title: Screenshot Stylekit: automated styling, redaction heuristics, and localization-safe overlays
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Define and implement a Screenshot Stylekit that produces brand-consistent, release-ready UI images from product builds with built-in redaction, smart cropping, and localization-safe overlays. The goal is a deterministic process designers and marketing can rely on for quickstart guides, docs, and release banners while reducing manual touchups and privacy risk.
acceptance_criteria: Stylekit can ingest full-resolution UI screenshots and output a standardized 16:9 hero, 4:3 doc image, and 1:1 avatar crop with consistent padding and shadow treatment
Sensitive text (emails, API keys, tokens, credit-card-like strings) is automatically redacted following the heuristic rules and replaced with localized placeholders
Locale-specific content (dates, currency, RTL layouts) is detected and the overlay engine can swap in neutral placeholder text or masked values without visual breakage
Figma export and a CLI tool exist for QA to batch-generate stylekit outputs from a directory of screenshots
Design sign-off on visual fidelity and marketing approves the first release batch (release-2025.03)
proposed_workflow_steps: 1) Ingest: Accept screenshot inputs (png/jpg) with metadata (build tag, route, locale) via a small uploader service or local CLI
2) Parse: Run OCR + DOM snapshot heuristic to identify text blocks, form fields, and identifiable PII candidates
3) Apply masks: Replace detected sensitive spans with neutral placeholders or blurred masks according to policy
4) Crop & Frame: Generate multiple aspect ratios using anchor heuristics (primary CTA, title line, user avatar) and ensure consistent brand margins
5) Overlay locale-safe placeholders: For detected locale-specific tokens (dates, currency), render templated replacements that match locale directionality
6) Render & Export: Apply brand layer (rounded corners, subtle drop shadow, border color), output optimized PNG and WebP, and upload artifacts to Drive and the design review board
7) Post-process QA: Run visual diff against golden examples and flag any image that exceeds a perceptual-diff threshold for manual review
redaction_heuristics: Regex patterns for common PII: email, phone, credit-card-like numeric sequences, UUIDs, and common API token prefixes (partial match with confidence threshold)
OCR confidence threshold: only redact OCR-detected text with >= 0.7 confidence; lower confidences are flagged for review
DOM alignment check: prioritize DOM-sourced labels when available (from e2e snapshots) to reduce false-positive redaction
Masking policy: short identifiers => replace with fixed-length block (e.g., ****-****), long tokens => blurred gradient over entire token
Do not redact: purely decorative text (e.g., sample lorem items defined in mock data lists) — detect via training set and allow whitelist
cropping_and_layout_rules: Primary crop anchors: CTA centroid, main heading baseline, or top-left primary content depending on route type
Minimum readable text size: ensure resulting crop keeps heading text at >= 18px visual size at target export width
Safe zones: maintain 48px brand margin for hero assets; 24px for in-doc screenshots
Fallback crop: center crop + scale if heuristics fail to identify anchors
Variant generation: output three sizes (hero-16x9, doc-4x3, thumb-1x1) with consistent visual treatment
localization_considerations: RTL support: mirror overlays and align placeholders to the reading edge; ensure masks follow mirrored bounding boxes
Locale-aware placeholders: replace dates and currencies with neutral but plausible formats per locale (e.g., 14 Apr 2025 vs 04/14/2025)
Text expansion allowance: designs must reserve +25% horizontal room for languages like German or Portuguese
Font fallback: use system-neutral fallback stack consistent with brand and test for glyph coverage in major target locales
Language detection: prefer DOM locale tag when provided; otherwise fall back to Unicode script heuristics from OCR
quality_and_qa_checklist: Visual diff (pixel and perceptual) against golden images
Manual spot check for first 50 images per release across locales
Verify no live-looking API keys, emails, or phone numbers remain in exported assets
Accessibility: contrast check for overlay text and placeholder labels
Export size and format: hero exports must be <= 250KB WebP when possible
open_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use a combined OCR+DOM approach vs DOM-only. Tradeoff: OCR increases recall for images from customer sandboxes but adds complexity and false positives; chosen hybrid approach to improve coverage.

Decision: Full token masking vs placeholder substitution. Tradeoff: placeholders preserve layout better, but masking minimizes risk of accidental leak; chosen policy uses placeholder substitution for short identifiers and full mask for token-like strings.

Decision: Perform language normalization vs preserve original locale text. Tradeoff: Normalization guarantees consistent branding in screenshots but loses fidelity to the user experience. We'll normalize only for marketing assets, keep original for product docs where exactness matters.
